articles.title: Watch: Moment part of Brighton's historic West Pier collapses
articles.summary: Footage taken during Storm Austen shows a section of the famous landmark battered by large waves and collapsing into the water.
articles.body:
A section of Brighton's historic West Pier has collapsed into the sea during the wet and windy weather brought by Storm Austen.

In footage obtained by the BBC, one side of the famous landmark in the East Sussex city can be seen falling into the water as it is battered by large waves.

The pier - which first opened in 1866 - attracted two million visitors at its peak, though its popularity declined after World War Two. While it was closed to the public in 1975, the increasingly ruined structure has become a symbol of Brighton for some.

Major sections fell into the sea during storms in late 2002, while two separate fires the following year destroyed most of what remained. Subsequent storms have destroyed its iron frame even further.

articles.title: The best N95 masks to protect against airborne viruses
articles.summary: NIOSH-approved N95 respirators are the most protective type of face mask, according to the CDC. Doctors explain how to shop for them.
articles.body: Out of all the different face masks you can wear, N95 respirators are the most protective, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). They’re designed to filter out at least 95% of small and large airborne particles, and they fit tightly against your face to reduce gaps around the sides, chin and nose area. Plus, N95s are regulated in the United States by the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), making them easier to shop for compared to similar international respirators like KN95s and KF94s. (Most people use “mask” and “respirator” interchangeably, but when the CDC and medical professionals say “respirator,” they specifically mean fitted face coverings with certified filtration, like N95s, KN95s and KF94s). I talked to medical experts about how to vet N95 masks, how these respirators differ from other disposable face coverings and when to wear them. I also compiled highly rated NIOSH-approved N95s that are available to buy online. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best N95 masks While many N95s meet NIOSH’s requirements, the CDC recommends leaving surgical-grade masks for medical professionals. Excluding those options, I compiled highly rated NIOSH-approved N95 masks you can shop online. Note that some N95s come packaged together, while others are individually wrapped. All the masks listed below have an adjustable nose bridge and two headstraps. 3M’s Aura foldable N95 respirator has a three-panel design and is made to be low profile around the nose and eye area to accommodate glasses. They come in a pack of 10 or 20, depending on the retailer. You can purchase Shawmut N95 respirators in a pack of 20 or 240. The masks are built with a piece of foam that lines the inside of the adjustable nose piece, which helps reduce eyeglass from fogging up. You can fold these N95s from Honeywell totally flat when you're not using them. Their adjustable nose clip has a foam cushion that helps create a tight seal against the face. Masks come in a pack of 20. The pouch design of these N95s creates a large breathing chamber, making it easier to talk while wearing the respirators, according to the brand. They come in a pack of 50. DemeTech’s N95s are designed with five layers of material and fold flat when they’re not in use. They come in a pack of 20. How I picked the best N95 masks Here’s what I kept in mind to curate this list of N95 masks: NIOSH approval: Since N95 masks are regulated by NIOSH, you should only purchase those listed on the agency’s list of approved models. “When NIOSH gives an N95 its stamp of approval, it means the respirator has met very specific requirements for testing,” says Dr. Stella Hines, an associate professor in the Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine at the University of Maryland School of Medicine. “It’s a quality assurance indicator that the respirator will perform as expected.” All NIOSH-approved N95s adhere to specific performance and quality requirements, including the ability to filter out at least 95% of large and very small particles (0.3 microns in size).Appropriate markings: Specific markings on an N95 mask indicate that it’s NIOSH-approved. These include identifying information verified using NIOSH’s Certified Equipment List, filter designations, model numbers and more.Features: According to experts, N95 masks should have two straps that go around your head and an adjustable wire nose bridge to help ensure that the mask fits tightly against your face. Never buy N95s made with exhaust ports, which holds true for all face masks, says Dr. David Rempel, a professor in the Department of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco.Shape: N95 masks come in cup, flat fold and duckbill shapes. Experts recommend picking whichever you find the most comfortable because one isn’t better than the other. It comes down to personal preference.Type: N95 respirators labeled as ‘surgical’ or ‘medical’ should be prioritized for healthcare workers, according to the CDC. A standard N95 mask is sufficient for the general public. How are you supposed to wear N95 masks? Regardless of the type of mask you wear, it won’t protect you or the people around you unless you wear it correctly. Make sure your mask completely covers your mouth and nose and fits tightly against your face to prevent gaps around the sides of the mask, nose and chin, according to the CDC. “N95 respirators will provide the regulated, expected level of protection to the wearer only if there’s a good seal to the face,” says Hines. “You want a good seal so that all of the air that’s breathed in is pulled in through the mask body. That’s where all the filtration of particles and microbial contaminants occurs.” You can do an at-home leak test with an N95 by putting it on and breathing out, says Rempel. If you can feel the air under your chin or around your eyes, it’s not tight enough. And if your glasses fog up while wearing an N95, there’s leakage and it’s not tight enough, says Hines. All masks and models fit differently, and features like an adjustable nose bridge help you improve the fit of your mask, as do mask fitters or braces, according to the CDC. Using a fitter or brace is especially a good idea for people with facial hair, which can make it difficult to achieve a tight fit. When should you wear a face mask? There’s no nationwide mask wearing mandate in the United States, so it can be tricky to decide when you should wear one. Here’s what experts recommend — and remember, wearing a mask can help reduce the transmission of illnesses like the flu, RSV and the common cold, not just Covid-19. In crowded indoor spaces where you spend more than 15 to 20 minutes: Examples include concerts, grocery stores, classrooms and offices, as well as transportation hubs like airports and train stations, says Dr. Carl Fichtenbaum, a professor of clinical medicine at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine. Wearing a face mask while traveling on a crowded plane, train or bus is also a good idea, he says.When you’re sick: You’re at the highest risk for transmitting a virus when you have a fever, so you should stay home, says Dr. Sharon Nachman, chief of the division of pediatric infectious diseases at Stony Brook Children’s Hospital. Once your fever gets better, or if you’re just coughing and sneezing, wear a mask if you absolutely have to go out in public, she says. Doing so makes it less likely that you’ll spread germs to others.If you’re at a higher risk for infection: This applies to those 65 and older, those with pre-existing medical conditions, previous infections, or those who take medications that may weaken the immune system, says Fichtenbaum.When there’s high levels of illness in your community: The CDC has Covid-19, flu and RSV trackers online that are open to the public, which Nachman recommends bookmarking. You can enter a zip code and see how present each illness is in your community or those you’re traveling to. If positivity is trending upward, that’s a sign that you should consider wearing a mask, especially in crowded indoor public spaces, says Nachman. Meet our health experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. David Rempel is a professor in the Department of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco.Dr. Stella Hines is an associate professor in the Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine at the University of Maryland School of Medicine. Dr. Carl Fichtenbaum is a professor of clinical medicine at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine.Dr. Sharon Nachman is the chief of the division of pediatric infectious diseases at Stony Brook Children’s Hospital. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has written about face masks since 2020, including articles about KN95s, N95s, disposable face masks and kid’s face masks. To write this article, I interviewed four doctors about how to shop for N95 masks and researched face coverings using resources from the CDC and NIOSH. I also recommended NIOSH-approved N95 masks to buy that meet expert guidance. articles.title: Cleveland Police yet to receive £2m after A66 crash, says commissioner
articles.summary: Cleveland Police and Crime Commissioner Matt Storey says it has been nearly two months since force was promised the cash.
articles.body:
A police force has still not received the £2m it was promised by the government in the wake of a car crash that led to the deaths of seven people, including two police officers, the local police and crime commissioner (PCC) says.

Cleveland PCC Matt Storey said Cleveland Police was still waiting for the extra funding promised by the home secretary in August.

Shabana Mahmood pledged the cash in light of challenges faced by the force following the deaths, which followed a pursuit on the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on 22 August. Five young men were also killed.

The Home Office said the force would receive the £2m it had been promised by the end of November.

During the fatal crash, a Volkswagen Passat in which the five young men were travelling hit an oncoming marked Cleveland Police vehicle on the dual carriageway near Middlesbrough at about 03:39 BST.

Officers PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died at the scene.

The occupants of the VW Passat, which was travelling the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, and 17-year-olds Theo Rae and Cole Robert Worthy - were also killed.

On the morning of the crash, Cleveland Police said it received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously around the town and a Volvo XC60 had been seen ramming properties.

Further arrests were subsequently made in connection with organised crime, including the following weekend after another vehicle ramming.

Storey called for the immediate release of the £2m but also said policing costs linked to the crash, which had led to the arrests of 50 people so far, were now forecast to exceed £5m.

"These are exceptional and unavoidable costs arising from utterly tragic and devastating circumstances," he said.

"They are not costs that should be borne locally or met from existing policing budgets."

The PCC also criticised the lack of a "substantive" communication from the government about Cleveland Police's long-term funding.

Storey said the current police funding model, which Mahmood had previously committed to reviewing, disadvantaged the Teesside force.

He said the upcoming Budget was a chance to "align resources more fairly with demand" and "place Cleveland on a sustainable footing".

The 50 arrests have come as part of a wider police operation against organised crime following the crash.

Fifteen people have been charged - 13 men and two women ranging in age from 19-45.

articles.title: Memorial do Clube da Esquina é alvo de vandalismo em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Placas do memorial foram cobertas por tinta vermelha na madrugada desta sexta-feira (23), em BH. Irmão de Lô Borges lamentou o vandalismo e fez um apelo contra a violência e a intolerância.
articles.summary: Placas do memorial do Clube da Esquina em BH foram vandalizadas com tinta vermelha sob suspeita de motivação política às vésperas das eleições.
articles.body:
O memorial do Clube da Esquina, no bairro Santa Tereza, na Região Leste de Belo Horizonte, foi vandalizado na madrugada desta sexta-feira (23). O espaço, localizado no cruzamento das ruas Divinópolis e Paraisópolis, teve placas em homenagem aos integrantes do movimento musical cobertas por tinta vermelha.

Câmeras de segurança de imóveis vizinhos registraram o momento em que um carro parou próximo ao memorial e uma pessoa jogou tinta sobre as placas. O ataque ocorreu a dois dias do segundo turno das eleições, e moradores suspeitam de motivação política após relatos de gritos de "Fora Lula" na região.

“É difícil até descrever o que a gente sente numa situação dessa.” O desabafo é de Yé Borges, irmão do músico Lô Borges, que lamentou o vandalismo e relembrou a importância da esquina para a história da música brasileira.

“Para mim é muito difícil. Vi nascer o Clube aqui na esquina. A gente jamais poderia imaginar que viraria uma referência no mundo. É muito triste, a violência não pode tomar conta das pessoas”, afirmou à TV Globo.

Yé também criticou a intolerância e defendeu o respeito às diferenças políticas .

“Vote em quem você quiser, mas não precisa agredir ninguém. Não precisamos chegar a essas vias de fato, isso é péssimo para a sociedade. É o legado que vamos deixar para os nossos filhos, para as nossas crianças: o ódio”, disse.

Apesar da indignação, o irmão de Lô Borges fez um apelo para que o episódio não seja respondido com mais violência.

“O ódio às vezes tenta me invadir, mas eu não deixo. O ódio gera ódio. A gente tem que emanar amor.”

Memorial na esquina das ruas Paraisópolis e Divinópolis, no bairro Santa Tereza, foi vandalizada na madrugada desta sexta-feira (23) — Foto: Imagens cedidas ao g1

Segundo a professora Graziela Viana, coordenadora de projeto que propõe tornar o Clube da Esquina em patrimônio cultural e imaterial do estado, câmeras de segurança de imóveis vizinhos registraram o momento em que um carro parou próximo ao memorial. Nas imagens, uma pessoa aparece com um pote de tinta e joga o conteúdo sobre as placas instaladas na esquina histórica.

Em entrevista à TV Globo , Graziela levantou a possibilidade de que o vandalismo tenha sido premeditado e esteja relacionado às eleições deste domingo (25).

A professora relatou que gritos de "Fora Lula" foram ouvidos na região, mas ressaltou que não há provas de que o ataque tenha motivação política.

“A gente não sabe se tem conotação política, porque foram ouvidos ‘Fora Lula’”, afirmou.

Ela destacou que a esquina é tradicionalmente um espaço de manifestações culturais, encontros e discussões, inclusive sobre política . Por isso, considera a possibilidade de o local ter sido escolhido intencionalmente.

O memorial fica em um dos pontos mais conhecidos do bairro Santa Tereza, onde surgiu o Clube da Esquina, movimento musical que ganhou projeção nacional e internacional a partir do trabalho de artistas como Milton Nascimento , Lô Borges , Beto Guedes e Toninho Horta .

Em dezembro de 2024, a casa localizada na esquina histórica foi reinaugurada após uma reforma. O imóvel passou a abrigar um espaço de coworking e atividades culturais. A revitalização também incluiu a instalação de um banco e de placas na calçada em homenagem aos músicos do Clube da Esquina.

O vandalismo ocorreu três dias antes do aniversário de Milton Nascimento , que completa 84 anos na próxima segunda-feira (26).

articles.title: Regras para levar power bank em voos: Teresina já apreendeu 80 | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudança em regras da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) estabelece diversas condições para o transporte do power bank.
articles.summary: As novas regras para levar power bank em voos da Anac limitam o transporte a bagagens de mão e estabelecem critérios de capacidade para evitar riscos de incêndio.
articles.body:
Aeroporto de Teresina já apreendeu cerca de 80 power bank inadequados para voo em 2026 — Foto: Reprodução

O Aeroporto de Teresina confirmou, nesta sexta-feira (23), que já foram apreendidos cerca de 80 carregadores portáteis fora das normas desde que a Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) passou a exigir novas regras para o transporte de power banks em voos , no mês de abril.

A Anac atualizou a lista de condições para o aparelho após registros de explosões e curtos-circuitos de carregadores desse tipo em voos no Brasil . As ocorrências causaram transtornos, como desvio de rota, em um dos casos .

Para transportar carregadores portáteis em voos, os passageiros devem seguir algumas regras. Os aparelhos só podem ser levados na bagagem de mão, não podem ser utilizados durante o voo e estão limitados a duas unidades por pessoa.

"As restrições têm como objetivo reduzir riscos associados às baterias de lítio, que podem apresentar superaquecimento e provocar incêndios quando danificadas ou submetidas a condições inadequadas", explicou o aeroporto da capital, em nota.

A gerência do aeroporto orienta que os viajantes verifiquem as informações dos aparelhos antes do embarque.

Veja a lista de condições para o transporte de power bank em voos:

São permitidos até dois carregadores portáteis por passageiro.

Capacidade: equipamentos de até 100 Wh são permitidos; os que possuem entre 100 Wh e 160 Wh exigem autorização prévia da companhia aérea.

O transporte deve ser feito na bagagem de mão. É proibido despachar o power bank.

O equipamento deve permanecer na bolsa, mochila ou item pessoal, em local de fácil acesso, conforme as orientações da companhia aérea. Não deve ser colocado no compartimento superior da aeronave.

Durante o voo, não é permitido recarregar o power bank a bordo. Também é importante observar as orientações da companhia aérea quanto ao uso do equipamento.

Proteção: os terminais devem estar protegidos contra curtos-circuitos, evitando contato com objetos metálicos ou outros materiais condutores.

articles.summary: Um acidente na Rodovia dos Bandeirantes interditou três faixas no km 52, em Jundiaí, provocando lentidão no sentido capital na tarde desta sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Acidente na rodovia Bandeirantes gera 7km de congestionamento em Jundiaí — Foto: CCO da Concessionária AUTOBAN

Um acidente entre um carro e uma carreta causou a interdição de três faixas de tráfego na Rodovia Bandeirantes (SP-348), sentido capital, no início da tarde desta sexta-feira (23), em Jundiaí (SP). Até a última atualização desta reportagem, o trecho registrava 7 km de congestionamento.

O acidente foi por volta das 13h40 e o trabalho de liberação da via durou cerca de uma hora. Os veículos foram retirados para o canteiro central às 14h40.

Não há informações sobre o estado de saúde dos motoristas do carro e da carreta e se houve a necessidade de atendimento médico para alguma vítima.

articles.title: Thomas Markle é investigado por posse de imagens de abuso infantil | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação nas Filipinas começou após meio-irmão de Meghan entregar à polícia evidências das acusações; Thomas Markle nega as denúncias
articles.summary: Thomas Markle nega acusações de abuso sexual infantil após denúncia feita pelo próprio filho às autoridades das Filipinas; Meghan Markle se diz profundamente abalada.
articles.body:
Thomas Markle, pai da duquesa de Sussex, em entrevista à emissora britânica ITV (arquivo). — Foto: Good Morning Britain/ITV handout via Reuters

As autoridades das Filipinas estão investigando Thomas Markle , pai de Meghan, esposa do príncipe Harry, do Reino Unido, após acusações de que ele possuía imagens de abuso sexual infantil, informou nesta sexta-feira o subsecretário de Justiça das Filipinas.

"Nossa força-tarefa de combate ao tráfico e ao abuso e exploração sexual de crianças on-line (OSAEC) em Cebu está atualmente investigando o caso", disse Nicholas Ty, subsecretário de Justiça das Filipinas, à Reuters.

A Reuters não conseguiu entrar imediatamente em contato com Thomas Markle para pedir um comentário, mas o jornal britânico "Daily Mail" o citou dizendo que as acusações contra ele eram falsas e "mentiras doentias".

Meghan, que é americana, casou-se em 2018 com o filho mais novo do rei Charles. Em um comunicado, ela disse estar "profundamente abalada" com as acusações , publicadas pela primeira vez pelo jornal britânico "The Sun" nesta sexta-feira (23).

Meghan afirmou em seu comunicado que sabia das acusações contra seu pai, de 82 anos, desde 2018 e que havia impedido que ele tivesse contato com seus filhos, Archie, de 7 anos, e Lilibet, de 5, para protegê-los .

Ela não mantém contato com o pai desde o período que antecedeu seu casamento em 2018. Dias antes da cerimônia, Thomas Markle disse que não compareceria por motivos de saúde, depois de admitir anteriormente que havia posado para fotos de paparazzi.

O ministro do Interior das Filipinas, Jonvic Remulla, disse à Reuters que foi o filho de Markle, meio-irmão de Meghan, também chamado Thomas, quem forneceu à polícia evidências das acusações , incluindo um laptop, confirmando detalhes publicados pelo "The Sun".

O pai de Meghan, que viveu por algum tempo em Cebu, nas Filipinas, agora estaria de volta aos Estados Unidos, acrescentou Remulla.

A duquesa de Sussex, Meghan Markle, em evento na Abadia de Westminster, no Reino Unido, em novembro de 2019 — Foto: Matt Dunham/AP/Arquivo

Meghan disse que lhe mostraram uma carta enviada à polícia britânica em 2018 com acusações "perturbadoras e preocupantes" contra seu pai, acrescentando que foi informada de que elas estavam sendo investigadas.

A polícia britânica disse estar ciente de "relatos da imprensa de que agentes do Comando de Proteção Especializada e da Realeza da Polícia Metropolitana estiveram envolvidos no encaminhamento de uma carta em 2018".

"Estamos realizando investigações internas na tentativa de confirmar isso", disse um porta-voz da Polícia Metropolitana.

Meghan afirmou estar "profundamente abalada pelas notícias que vieram à tona nas últimas 24 horas, e meus pensamentos estão com todas as crianças que possam ter sido vítimas de violência".

"Minha mais sincera esperança é que a justiça seja plenamente feita e que a prioridade continue sendo a segurança e a proteção de crianças inocentes", disse ela.

O "The Sun" também informou que o filho de Thomas Markle havia entrado em contato com o FBI, nos Estados Unidos, por causa das acusações. O FBI não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

Harry e Meghan e seus filhos se mudaram para a Inglaterra em agosto, após viverem na Califórnia por seis anos.

articles.title: O peixe protegido por lei que teve captura autorizada em MS; entenda  | G1
articles.standfirst: A liberação da captura está autorizada apenas para os pesquisadores, a pesca predatória da espécie continua proibida nos rios de Mato Grosso do Sul.
articles.summary: A liberação da captura está autorizada apenas para os pesquisadores, a pesca predatória da espécie continua proibida nos rios de Mato Grosso do Sul.
articles.body:
Dourado. — Foto: Divulgação/Governo de Mato Grosso do Sul.

O Instituto de Meio Ambiente de Mato Grosso do Sul (Imasul) autorizou a captura, o manejo e o transporte de dourados para uma pesquisa científica que vai avaliar os efeitos da proibição da pesca da espécie no estado.

O objetivo é reunir dados que ajudem a decidir se a restrição, válida até 31 de março de 2027, deve ser prorrogada. Apesar da liberação para fins científicos, a pesca da espécie continua proibida nos rios de Mato Grosso do Sul.

A autorização foi publicada nesta sexta-feira (23) no Diário Oficial do Estado. A pesquisa faz parte do projeto interinstitucional Estado da arte do Dourado – Salminus brasiliensis em Mato Grosso do Sul .

O estudo reúne pesquisadores da Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária (Embrapa Pantanal), da Universidade Estadual de Mato Grosso do Sul (UEMS), da Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul (UFMS), da Universidade Federal da Grande Dourados (UFGD) e da Universidade Estadual de Maringá (UEM).

Segundo a portaria, a captura será realizada nas bacias dos rios Paraguai e Paraná, em território sul-mato-grossense. Os peixes serão analisados para ampliar o conhecimento sobre a biologia da espécie, a atividade pesqueira e as mudanças na população de dourados.

O documento também limita o sacrifício de peixes e a coleta de materiais biológicos, como otólitos (estruturas do ouvido interno dos peixes), escamas e tecidos. Esses procedimentos deverão ocorrer apenas na quantidade necessária para as análises previstas no estudo.

A pesquisa será coordenada por representantes das instituições participantes. Os pesquisadores deverão entregar relatórios parciais e um documento final ao Imasul, conforme o cronograma do acordo de cooperação técnica firmado em 2025.

A autorização vale até o fim do acordo ou de eventuais prorrogações.

A proibição da pesca do dourado em Mato Grosso do Sul foi prorrogada em março de 2025, após aprovação da Assembleia Legislativa. A lei foi sancionada pelo governador Eduardo Riedel (PP) e mantém a restrição até 31 de março de 2027.

A legislação proíbe a captura, o embarque, o transporte, a venda, o processamento e a industrialização do peixe no estado.

Entre as exceções estão a pesca na modalidade pesque e solte, o consumo próprio por pescadores profissionais e ribeirinhos e a utilização de exemplares criados em cativeiro.

A lei também prevê a realização de estudos científicos e econômicos durante o período de restrição. Os resultados devem ser apresentados até 28 de fevereiro de 2027.

A data marca o prazo previsto para a divulgação das conclusões em uma audiência pública na Assembleia Legislativa. O encontro também deverá avaliar os efeitos e a eficácia da proibição.

A autorização concedida pelo Imasul atende à etapa de pesquisa prevista na legislação. A captura de dourados está limitada ao estudo científico e não libera a pesca da espécie para a população.

articles.summary: Segundo a empresa, ferramenta foi mais de duas vezes mais precisa que médicos generalistas ao analisar mais de 300 casos complexos; próximo teste será na triagem de pacientes em pronto-socorro.
articles.body:
Microsoft diz que sua IA superou médicos em testes de diagnóstico — Foto: REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Ilustração/Foto de arquivo

Pesquisadores da Microsoft afirmam ter desenvolvido uma ferramenta de IA que foi mais de duas vezes mais precisa do que médicos generalistas ao diagnosticar casos complexos em testes. O resultado foi apresentado em um estudo publicado nesta quinta-feira (22) na revista Science.

A ferramenta analisa os casos em etapas, de forma semelhante à investigação feita por um médico. Primeiro, decide quais perguntas fazer sobre o histórico do paciente e quais informações do exame físico são relevantes. Depois, escolhe os exames necessários, avalia os resultados e solicita novos testes, se preciso.

Ao longo desse processo, a IA atualiza suas hipóteses e os próximos passos. Um sistema chamado "orquestrador" coordena a análise e simula um grupo de especialistas que trabalham juntos para chegar ao diagnóstico.

Nos testes, a ferramenta recebeu mais de 300 casos médicos incomuns e difíceis de diagnosticar . Segundo os pesquisadores, ela foi mais de duas vezes mais precisa na investigação e na identificação do diagnóstico do que médicos generalistas que podiam consultar livros e a internet.

A IA também superou médicos em simulações baseadas em registros de uma grande base de dados de atendimentos em pronto-socorro.

Segundo os autores, os modelos de IA médica existentes costumam analisar de uma só vez os sintomas, os resultados de exames laboratoriais e as imagens do paciente. As comparações com médicos geralmente usam questões de múltipla escolha.

"A IA ficou muito boa em acertar 100% dessas questões", disse Dominic King, vice-presidente corporativo da área de saúde da Microsoft AI. "Mas, é claro, isso não corresponde ao mundo real. Nenhum paciente jamais chegou ao meu consultório com um resumo bem organizado".

Os pesquisadores também afirmam que os processos de diagnóstico conduzidos pela ferramenta custaram menos do que os realizados pelos médicos.

"Não estamos medindo apenas a precisão dos sistemas. Também medimos o cuidado e o critério com que eles conduzem uma investigação diagnóstica", disse Harsha Nori, chefe de IA da Microsoft AI Health.

A próxima etapa será testar a capacidade da ferramenta de fazer a triagem de pacientes em salas de espera de pronto-socorro, em parceria com o Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, em Boston.

articles.title: Incêndio em fábrica em Jacareí atinge depósito e deixa um ferido | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo atingiu cerca de 150 m² de um depósito de 5 mil m²; vítima foi encaminhada ao pronto-socorro com suspeita de intoxicação por inalação de fumaça.
articles.summary: Incêndio em fábrica em Jacareí atingiu 150 m² de um depósito da Inylbra e um homem foi levado ao pronto-socorro com suspeita de intoxicação por fumaça.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu parte de um depósito de uma fábrica de carpetes na tarde desta sexta-feira (23), em Jacareí , no interior de São Paulo.

Um homem, com cerca de 30 anos, foi socorrido com suspeita de intoxicação por inalação de fumaça e encaminhado ao pronto-socorro , de acordo com apuração do repórter João Mota, da Rede Vanguarda.

Segundo informações do Corpo de Bombeiros, cerca de 150 metros quadrados foram atingidos pelo fogo em um depósito com área total de 5 mil metros quadrados.

A ocorrência foi registrada na avenida Getúlio Dorneles Vargas, no Jardim Califórnia. Segundo uma moradora que enviou um vídeo à reportagem, o incêndio atingiu a fábrica da Inylbra, que produz tapetes e carpetes. As causas do incêndio serão apuradas.

articles.title: Trump ataca Abdul El-Sayed e o chama de 'jihadista' antes das midterms | G1
articles.standfirst: Há semanas, os republicanos afirmam que Abdul El-Sayed, que concorre ao Senado pelo Michigan, tem ligações com a Irmandade Muçulmana, um grupo considerado terrorista pelo Departamento de Estado.
articles.summary: Republicanos afirmam que Abdul El-Sayed, que concorre ao Senado pelo Michigan, tem ligações com a Irmandade Muçulmana, grupo considerado terrorista pelos EUA. Ele nega.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, durante comício no Kansas em 19 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , fez um ataque direto a um candidato democrata ao Senado pelo estado de Michigan nesta sexta-feira (23).

Faltando duas semanas para as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA , Trump chamou Abdul El-Sayed de "jihadista doentio e violento" em declaração à imprensa na Casa Branca .

O presidente americano também acusou o candidato democrata de pertencer a um grupo chamado Irmandade Muçulmana, o que já foi negado por El-Sayed, e afirmou que ele esconde que seu nome do meio é Mohammed.

"Ele é um farsantezinho, e tudo nele é falso. É um mentiroso. Fala de todas essas coisas como se fosse moderado, mas não é. Ele é um jihadista. Um jihadista doentio e violento, e não tem lugar no nosso governo", falou Trump.

Abdul El-Sayed e Mike Rogers, candidatos ao Senado por Michigan — Foto: REUTERS/Rebecca Cook

A disputa entre Abdul El-Sayed e o ex-deputado republicano Mike Rogers por uma cadeira ao Senado é citada pela imprensa americana como uma das mais acirradas das midterms .

Há semanas, os republicanos afirmam que El-Sayed tem ligações com a Irmandade Muçulmana, um grupo considerado terrorista pelo Departamento de Estado . Mike Rogers mencionou antigas postagens de redes sociais da meia-irmã de El-Sayed, nas quais ela afirma que sua mãe esteve envolvida com a organização na década de 1970.

Além de negar qualquer ligação com o grupo, El-Sayed afirmou que não foi criado pela mãe. Seus pais se divorciaram quando ele tinha 3 anos, e ele viveu com o pai e a madrasta.

Durante um debate televisionado entre os dois esta semana, Rogers questionou a lealdade do democrata aos Estados Unidos:

"Se você pretende se candidatar ao Senado dos Estados Unidos, precisamos saber: você está a favor da América ou está a favor desses grupos terroristas no exterior?" .

El-Sayed, que é filho de imigrantes egípcios e, se eleito, será o primeiro muçulmano a ser designado para o Senado dos EUA, respondeu chamando a pergunta de vergonhosa:

"É algo bastante indigno de você, Mike. Tenho orgulho da América. Tenho orgulho de ser americano. Tenho orgulho da nossa Constituição, que garante a todos nós o direito de orar como quisermos".

No começo do mês, em entrevista a um programa da NBC News, o democrata acusou os republicanos de fomentarem a islamofobia ao se referirem a ele pelo nome completo e insistirem em sua ligação com o terrorismo:

"A única estratégia de Rogers é apontar para mim, para o meu nome e para a minha fé, e dizer que somos diferentes. E que você deve suspeitar das pessoas simplesmente porque elas são diferentes de você na forma como oram. É realmente vergonhoso. Mas ele não tem ideias. Ele não se importa de verdade em resolver problemas. Ele se importa com o poder".

Pesquisadores e estrategistas políticos afirmaram à Reuters que a estratégia visa convencer eleitores judeus e negros da região de Detroit, que apoiaram a adversária de El-Sayed nas primárias democratas, Haley Stevens, a não votarem em El-Sayed.

No momento, a disputa é considerada indefinida por analistas políticos independentes, com pesquisas mostrando El-Sayed com uma vantagem média de 2,6 pontos percentuais, de acordo com o site RealClearPolling.com.

articles.title: Marília Gabriela se emociona em peça com filho em São José dos Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Jornalista e o filho, o ator Theodoro Cochrane, apresentam o espetáculo 'A Última Entrevista de Marília Gabriela' nesta sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24), no Teatro Colinas.
articles.summary: Marília Gabriela e Theodoro Cochrane apresentam a peça "A Última Entrevista de Marília Gabriela" no Teatro Colinas, em São José dos Campos, com reflexões sobre a maternidade.
articles.body:
A atriz e jornalista Marília Gabriela e o filho dela, o ator Theodoro Cochrane, apresentam o espetáculo "A Última Entrevista de Marília Gabriela" nesta sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24), às 20h, no Teatro Colinas, em São José dos Campos.

Em entrevista ao vivo ao repórter Guilherme Machado, no Link Vanguarda , Marília Gabriela falou sobre a relação entre mães e filhos e revelou qual pergunta considera fundamental fazer ao próprio filho.

“'Você me ama? Me ama de verdade?' Eu tenho vontade de chorar quando falo, sou besta. A gente vai ficando velho e chora mais fácil. É isso: 'você me ama, meu filho?'. Porque tem toda a carreira da mãe . (...)Tem a convivência, tem a criação, tem a culpa de ter trabalhado enquanto o filho crescia, tem tudo envolvido. É uma relação, é fortíssima", disse.

Ao devolver a pergunta ao filho, Marília Gabriela quis saber o que ele gostaria de perguntar à mãe. Theodoro Cochrane respondeu que gostaria de saber se ela sente orgulho dele. “Você tem orgulho de mim?”, disse o ator.

Para Theodoro, o reconhecimento materno tem um significado importante, mesmo para quem já passou por diferentes experiências e processos de autoconhecimento.

“A nossa maior referência é de quem a gente saiu, ou não saiu, mas saiu mesmo, intelectualmente que seja. E a gente dar orgulho para essa pessoa é uma realização mesmo”, afirmou.

Marília Gabriela se emociona ao falar sobre relação com o filho, com quem se apresenta em São José dos Campos: 'É fortíssima' — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Espetáculo aborda relação entre mãe e filho

A peça "A Última Entrevista de Marília Gabriela" é uma comédia dramática que se passa durante um programa de entrevistas ao vivo no teatro. Na trama, ficção e realidade se misturam, e o que deveria ser apenas uma entrevista se transforma em um jogo que revela diferentes aspectos da relação entre mãe e filho.

A montagem aborda temas como feminismo, conflitos geracionais, etarismo e os limites entre a vida pública e a privada.

Sem a chamada quarta parede, que separa os atores do público, o espetáculo também convida os espectadores a participar da apresentação, inclusive no tradicional bate-bola, marca registrada de Marília Gabriela.

articles.title: Caminhão carregado com mercadorias pega fogo na BR-222 em Santa Inês | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo transportava peças de veículos, vidros e outros materiais que seriam distribuídos em comércios da cidade. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: Veículo transportava peças de veículos, vidros e outros materiais que seriam distribuídos em comércios da cidade. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.body:
Um caminhão carregado com mercadorias como peças de veículos, vidros e outros materiais pegou fogo na manhã desta sexta-feira (23), na BR-222, nas proximidades do povoado Barros Filho, em Santa Inês , a 249 km de São Luís. Ninguém ficou ferido.

O veículo seguia no sentido da cidade de Santa Luzia para Santa Inês quando o motorista percebeu fumaça saindo da carroceria. Ele parou o caminhão em uma área próxima à rodovia, e moradores da região tentaram ajudar a conter as chamas usando baldes de água.

O motorista também tentou apagar o fogo, mas as chamas se espalharam pela carroceria e atingiram a cabine do veículo.

Os materiais que o veículo transportava seriam distribuídos em estabelecimentos comerciais de Santa Inês. A carga foi destruída, e o veículo teve perda total.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e esteve no local, mas, quando a equipe chegou, o fogo já havia destruído o caminhão. As causa do incêndio serão investigadas.

articles.title: Jovens feridas em grave acidente que matou estudante recebem alta  | G1
articles.standfirst: Paloma Binotto, de 22 anos, dirigia carro que bateu contra caminhão, em Araras, e morreu no local. Passageiras, de 22 e 23, que estavam com ela, saíram do hospital nesta sexta (23).
articles.summary: Paloma Binotto, de 22 anos, conduzia o carro que bateu contra caminhão na SP-191, em Araras, e morreu no local. Passageiras, de 22 e 23, que estavam com ela, saíram do hospital.
articles.body:
As duas jovens, de 22 e 23 anos, que ficaram feridas em uma colisão entre um carro e um caminhão , que causou a morte da estudante Paloma Novaes Binotto, de 22, na Rodovia Wilson Finardi (SP-191), em Araras , receberam alta hospitalar nesta sexta-feira (23).

O acidente ocorreu por volta das 11h51 de quinta-feira (22), na altura do km 32. Paloma, que conduzia o carro, não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu no local.

Heloisa Miranda Costa, de 22 anos, e Lívia de Menezes Christiano, de 23, eram passageiras do carro e foram socorridas e levadas à Santa Casa da cidade, onde permaneceram sob observação até a manhã desta sexta-feira. O motorista do caminhão envolvido na colisão não se feriu.

Conforme apurado pelo g1 , uma das passageiras feridas já saiu da Santa Casa de Araras. A outra segue na instituição aguardando o término da aplicação de antibiótico, mas também já está liberada.

Lívia mora em Artur Nogueira , cidade onde nasceu. Já Heloisa, nasceu em Limeira e, atualmente, mora em Engenheiro Coelho.

Grave acidente com morte de jovem aconteceu na Rodovia SP-191, em Araras (SP) — Foto: Redes Sociais e Gean Mendes/F5 Conchal

De acordo com o Centro de Controle Operacional (CCO) da Concessionária Intervias, que administra o trecho, o carro trafegava no sentido leste, quando, por motivos a serem esclarecidos, invadiu a faixa oeste, colidindo contra a lateral traseira do reboque da carreta.

Após o impacto, o carro imobilizou-se na faixa adicional leste, enquanto a carreta parou a aproximadamente 100 metros do local da colisão, no sentido oeste.

Grave acidente com morte de jovem aconteceu na Rodovia SP-191, em Araras (SP) — Foto: Gean Mendes/F5 Conchal

De acordo com o CCO da Intervias, uma pessoa que estava no carro morreu. Outras duas pessoas que estavam no mesmo veículo também ficaram feridas, uma em estado grave e a outra leve.

O condutor do caminhão afirmou à polícia que trafegava no sentido Araras para Conchal, quando a condutora do veículo teria iniciado manobra de ultrapassagem a outro caminhão no início da terceira faixa, ocasião em que teria invadido a pista contrária, provocando a colisão frontal.

Ainda de acordo com a concessionária, a perícia chegou ao local do acidente por volta das 14h05. Minutos depois, a funerária chegou para retirar o corpo da vítima.

Paloma Novaes Binotto, de 22 anos, morreu em grave acidente na SP-191, em Araras (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Natural de Artur Nogueira, Paloma tinha formação técnica em enfermagem e era especialista em vacinação. Em dezembro deste ano, ela iria concluir o período de estágio e o bacharelado de enfermagem na Fundação Hermínio Ometto (FHO) de Araras.

Ao g1 , o irmão Erick Novaes El Khatib, de 36 anos, contou que a vítima era uma "pessoa maravilhosa, sempre levando alegria e luz para todos". Ele ainda destacou a paixão da irmã pela enfermagem.

"Ela era muito querida por todos. Sempre foi apaixonada por cuidar de pessoas e fazia isso com maestria e muito amor. Um dom excepcional que ela tinha", comentou.

Segundo Erick, ainda não há informações sobre velório e sepultamento, mas deverão acontecer em Artur Nogueira.

Amigas e colegas de faculdade de Paloma prestaram homenagens nas redes sociais na noite de quinta. Beatriz Valencise disse não acreditar na tragédia e disse que, com certeza, a estudante "vai iluminar o céu com sua risada, seu sorriso contagiante".

"Obrigada por cada momento que passamos juntas. Desde o dia que te conheci, tive a certeza de que você era uma mulher iluminada! E vai continuar assim no meu coração... Obrigada por cada risada juntas, por cada procedimento que realizamos juntas, obrigada por ser você!", concluiu.

Já Amanda Timachi afirmou que "vamos terminar esse ciclo [da enfermagem] principalmente por você, que tanto nos encheu de alegria todos os dias".

A amiga Laysa Fogaça de Almeida lamentou o acidente. "Que dor. Que tragédia", escreveu. Depois, relembrou que Paloma foi sua "enfermeira particular e mais recentemente, madrinha de casamento".

Ana Luisa Maranho relatou estar "ainda tentando entender o porquê" e também destacou que a reta final de graduação será feito em homenagem à Paloma. "Obrigada por cada risada, conselho e apoio nessa etapa. Você sempre dizia 'olha lá em, ninguém sai desse grupo' e saiu assim, sem nem se despedir", completou.

Curso de enfermagem da FHO lamenta morte

Curso de enfermagem da FHO manifestou pesar pela morte de Paloma Novaes Binotto — Foto: Reprodução

Nas redes sociais, o curso de enfermagem da FHO lamentou a tragédia. Veja abaixo a nota de pesar:

"Com profundo pesar, o Curso de Enfermagem se despede de sua aluna, cuja partida deixa saudade e um vazio imensurável. Que Deus conforte os corações de seus familiares, amigos e de toda a nossa comunidade acadêmica. Paloma Binotto. Sua memória permanecerá para sempre em nós!"

articles.title: Máquina cai de balsa durante remoção de destroços de ponte em Linhares | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipamento era utilizado na retirada dos restos da estrutura que desabou em 2009. O acidente foi registrado em vídeo nesta quinta-feira (22).
articles.summary: Equipamento era utilizado na retirada dos restos da estrutura que desabou em 2009. O acidente foi registrado em vídeo nesta quinta-feira (22).
articles.body:
Uma máquina utilizada na remoção dos destroços da antiga Ponte Getúlio Vargas caiu de uma balsa no Rio Doce , em Linhares , no Norte do Espírito Santo, nesta quinta-feira (22). Não houve feridos. O acidente aconteceu durante os trabalhos de retirada dos restos da estrutura que desabou em 2009 .

O acidente foi registrado em um vídeo gravado da Ponte Joaquim Calmon. Nas imagens, é possível observar a balsa aparentemente danificada após a queda da máquina .

Em 2022, a Justiça Federal já tinha determinado a União e o Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes (Dnit) realizassem a demolição do trecho remanescente da estrutura e retirassem os destroços do Rio Doce.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Linhares, o equipamento era utilizado na remoção dos destroços, serviço sob responsabilidade do departamento nacional.

Já o Dnit declarou que a rodovia em questão é concedida e que as informações deveriam ser consultadas junto à concessionária responsável.

A Ecovias Capixaba, por sua vez, orientou o g1 a buscar mais informações junto ao Dnit, que realiza os trabalhos de demolição da antiga ponte no local.

Máquina caiu de uma balsa no Rio Doce, em Linhares — Foto: Redes Socias

O g1 também procurou Dnit para esclarecer as circunstâncias do acidente, informar se houve feridos e explicar como ficará o andamento dos trabalhos, mas não houve retorno até a publicação da reportagem.

O desabamento da Ponte Getúlio Vargas aconteceu no dia 19 de janeiro de 2009, quando cerca de 200 metros da estrutura da ponte caíram.

No acidente, duas mulheres caíram no Rio Doce. Uma conseguiu se salvar, mas a outra, a manicure Devanir Farias de Souza, que caminhava no local durante o desabamento, morreu.

Em 2022, a Justiça Federal determinou que o Dnit e a União demolissem o trecho remanescente da estrutura e retirassem os destroços do Rio Doce. A decisão atendeu a um pedido do Ministério Público Federal (MPF) . O processo destacou que as ruínas e os destroços da estrutura causavam riscos à navegação local e danos ao meio ambiente.

articles.title: Stepdad jailed for murdering Carla Georgescu on her birthday
articles.summary: Nathan Owens had a "longstanding sexual obsession" with his stepdaughter Carla Georgescu, a judge says.
articles.body:
A man who was "sexually obsessed" with his stepdaughter has been jailed for a minimum of 35 years for murdering her at her university flat on her 20th birthday.

Nathan Owens, 34, from Hartlepool, killed Carla Georgescu in her room at the University of Lancashire property in Preston in February and then staged the scene to make it look like she had taken her own life.

Judge Jacobs said Carla had been described as polite, kind, intelligent and articulate with "a very gentle way" but she had suffered "a horrific brutal attack".

He said Owens had a "longstanding sexual obsession with Carla" that was hidden from her and her mother.

The second-year student suffered knife wounds, including injuries where she tried to defend herself, internal injuries from a sexual assault and two "powerful blows to the head", the judge said.

Owens also attempted to strangle her, the court heard.

Nicholas Lumley KC, for the prosecution, told Preston Crown Court Carla was "thriving" at the University of Lancashire, and had planned to continue her studies at a high level, "working towards a doctorate".

He said she was "excitedly looking forward" to travelling to her home country of Romania to meet up with her first boyfriend.

Owens had pleaded guilty shortly before the trial to making and possessing indecent images of Carla when she was between the ages of two and four by superimposing her image on to sexualised pictures.

Lumley said Owens' offending was "pre-meditated, non consensual, violent and sustained" and that Carla would have been in "very great pain" when he sexually assaulted her.

The judge said he was "sure" that fatal violence was "part of the plan" if Carla were to resist the sexual attack that Owens had decided to carry out.

He said "the last 90 minutes of Carla's life are too horrendous to think about" but he said "it is likely and indeed to be hoped that at some point she became unconscious and so was not aware of everything that happened to her".

Owens had not shown any remorse, he said, and had denied injuring Carla in any way.

The judge said he had "taken victim blaming to its limit" by suggesting she may have taken her own life.

Carla's body was found in her room at the university's Ribble Hall on 5 February.

The trial saw CCTV footage of Owens having a meal with Carla and her mother in the days before she died and him going to her flat in the early hours of 4 February wrapped in a blanket.

Carla let him into the building at about 04:00 GMT after he lied about picking something up and he left an hour-and-a-half later, the court heard.

That CCTV footage of Carla letting Owens in was the last time she was seen alive, Lancashire Police said.

Owens subjected his stepdaughter to a violent and sexual assault as he strangled her.

He then staged the scene to look as if Carla had taken her own life and returned home as though nothing had happened, disposing of evidence on his route.

Detectives arrested him soon afterwards but he denied any involvement in Carla's death.

Owens chose not to give evidence at his trial.

Det Insp Pete Macdonald said: "Owens has taken Carla's life, but he has also changed her mum's completely.

"He has torn apart the family he was trusted to love.

articles.title: Woman at centre of Cornell University rape inquiry in 'constant fear', lawyer says
articles.summary: The woman, known anonymously as Jane Doe, alleged she was drugged and raped by several men on Cornell's campus.
articles.body:
The life of a woman who filed a lawsuit alleging she was drugged and raped at a Cornell University fraternity house has been completely upended, her lawyer has said.

Speaking to the BBC ahead of a hearing in the civil case on Friday in New York, her lawyer Thomas Giuffra said: "She feels under fire."

The woman, known anonymously as Jane Doe, is suing her former school and the fraternity over the alleged incident involving several men at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.

When the case went viral, a series of "I am Jane Doe" solidarity posts appeared, but there was a separate campaign aimed at unmasking her and defending the men, who have all denied any wrongdoing.

The men, who are also being sued by the woman, have not been charged with any crimes.

With initial proceedings now under way in the civil case, Giuffra told the BBC that these last few weeks have been "a very hard time" for his client, who isn't doing a lot beyond "surviving".

Her decision to sue was rooted in a desire for closure and to take power back, he said.

Giufrra visited Jane Doe this week and found that she hadn't been sleeping well – relying on medication to get rest.

Now in trauma therapy, he says she doesn't feel safe in her own home following malicious threats that were directed at her and her family.

After her address was published online without her consent, someone called in a fake emergency that led to police in full tactical gear drawing assault rifles on her father, her friend and her brother at their family home.

He added that despite this her resolve hadn't been shaken and she remains determined to overhaul the university system at Cornell, and across the country, to protect survivors.

Cornell University, after initially defending its disciplinary measures, acknowledged it fell short in its handling of Jane Doe's case.

After facing intense pressure, the college's president announced that fraternity parties would be suspended until the end of the academic year to allow for a thorough review to determine whether and how they can safely continue.

The school also said it would add sexual assault investigators to its police force.

Giuffra, however, says he is surprised that Cornell has not reached out to him and believes they have been focused solely on "damage control".

He says any agreement with Cornell to resolve the civil lawsuit will need to include "steps to ensure there are no more Jane Does" and if there are, that they are going to be supported.

The BBC contacted Cornell for comment who directed us to the university's previous statements and comments on its internal investigation in 2024.

New York's governor Kathy Hochul appointed a special prosecutor, New York's Attorney General Letitia James, to oversee a reopened investigation into whether criminal charges are warranted.

Giuffra expects it will take a long time to do a proper investigation but is concerned that they will be going after evidence that is now "stale".

"A lot of the communication was on Snapchat, Snapchat goes away," he told the BBC.

"The best time to get evidence is around the time of the crime and that just didn't happen."

However, Giuffra believes he can win the civil case against the university, the men and others, where the burden of proof is lower than a criminal case.

Civil cases require a preponderance of the evidence, that it's more likely than not it happened, while criminal cases require proof beyond a reasonable doubt.

Recent high profile cases have shown the way juries evaluate consent can be unpredictable.

"I wouldn't have taken the case if I didn't think it was a strong case that I could win and get her some closure."

articles.title: Serbia’s longtime leader faces biggest political test as students mount election challenge
articles.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned to run for prime minister, facing his biggest electoral challenge in 14 years by a political party founded by student protesters.
articles.body: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned from the presidency in September and is running for prime minister in parliamentary elections considered to be one of the most competitive elections for Serbia in recent memory. "I think this is certainly the biggest challenge for the former President in his 14-year rule," Helena Ivanov, associate fellow at the Henry Jackson Society, told Fox News Digital. "The student protesters have been able to capture the hearts and minds of people and keep the momentum going in a way that the established opposition was never able to do," Ivanov added. ANTI‑CORRUPTION PROTESTS HIT EUROPEAN NATION AS CALLS FOR NEW ELECTIONS GROW Serbian Foreign Minister Marko Djuric told Fox News Digital that he believes the student opposition is highly unlikely to win. "The people of Serbia have seen through them: years of criticism have not persuaded the public that they have a credible program or a serious plan for the country’s future," the foreign minister said. Djuric touted Serbia’s economy under Vucic and the Strategic Dialogue with the U.S., which he said will foster greater cooperation and new opportunities for Serbs. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital in June when he was still president, Vucic pointed to the country's economic growth as evidence of its transformation. "Our GDP was 32 billion (euros) when I became the prime minister," Vucic said. "This year it's going to be over 100 billion euros, which is $120 billion." Vucic first became prime minister in 2014 and president in 2017. In that same interview, he said the improving relationship between Washington and Belgrade was increasingly centered on economics, investment and technological cooperation and mutual conservative values. A bipartisan group of senators led by Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa., and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., introduced the Supporting the Rule of Law, Building Institutional Justice, and Accountability Act (SRBIJA) to address democratic backsliding in Serbia, promote the rule of law and accountability and improve the treatment of student-led civic protests. Most importantly, the legislation would condition future aid on a presidential certification that Serbia made "significant and sustained" efforts toward judicial accountability, press freedom and alignment with the EU and NATO. The bipartisan group of lawmakers, which also included Rep. Joe Wilson, R-S.C., and Rep. William Keating, D-Mass., took aim at President Vucic and his time in power. EXCLUSIVE: SERBIAN PRESIDENT VUČIĆ SAYS SUPPORT FOR US 'SURGED' UNDER TRUMP, INVITES HIM TO VISIT BELGRADE There are growing concerns from Congress and observers that the election will take place in a hostile environment and efforts to discredit and undermine the election are already underway. Others fear the current government might not respect the outcome of the election if the Student List were to win. Vucic had served as president of Serbia since 2017 and previously as prime minister from 2014 to 2017, but was term limited under the constitution. His exit from the presidency created the opportunity for him to remain in power by returning as prime minister. Vucic resigned from the presidency and dissolved parliament in September, setting the stage for the snap election on Oct. 25. As president, analysts say he has always straddled the geopolitical line between East and West, seeking European legitimacy and launching EU accession talks in 2014 while also maintaining close ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin even after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Unlike previous elections, the student-led opposition garnered significant attention to their cause and mobilized popular support, becoming a legitimate political contender out of a spontaneous protest movement. Serbia has been roiled by student-led anti-corruption protests since November 2024, demanding justice and accountability after the deaths of 16 people following the collapse of a railway station in the town of Novi Sad. One of the largest protests in Serbia’s history took place on March 15, 2025, with nearly 350,000 people gathered in Slavija Square in central Belgrade. ZELENSKYY WARNS RUSSIA WANTS TO CAUSE 'EXPLOSION' IN THE BALKANS The protesters criticized the Vucic government for failing to hold anyone accountable for the canopy disaster as the government continued its heavy-handed crackdown on demonstrators. None of the original demands of the protesters were met, so the students turned to electoral politics to enact change the Serbian political opposition was never able to achieve. The Student List, as the opposition is known, consists of a wide swath of civil society actors, many of whom come from the ranks of academia, but does not include anyone from Serbia’s traditional opposition parties that struggled to challenge Vucic and his ruling Serbian Progressive Party in the past. The group operates in a decentralized manner and does not have an official leader. Their main priorities are to tackle corruption and promote transparency and the rule of law. Filip Ubović, a student from the University of Belgrade and protest participant on the ground in Belgrade, has spoken with Fox News Digital over the course of the year-long protests. SERBIA, CAUGHT BETWEEN EUROPE AND RUSSIA, COULD MOVE ONE STEP CLOSER TO NORMALIZING RELATIONS WITH KOSOVO Ubović said he joined the protests because he was fed up with the current state of his country. This was the first opportunity, Ubovic said, to do something tangible, instead of just complaining. "People had enough for quite some time but decided to fully embrace us because we are ‘their kids’, we are young, we are not professional politicians, we do not have a single face representing us, and we are very professional and principled," Ubovic said. Ivana Stradner of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies told Fox News Digital that corruption has held back democracy in the Balkans and progress for its people for a while. "Corruption doesn’t just steal public money; it steals an entire generation’s future. Young people in Serbia and Albania are taking to the streets demanding accountability and a better future. The U.S. should pay attention, not out of charity, but strategic self-interest," Stradner said. ‘VOTERS GET TO CHOOSE — JUST NOT THE RESULT’: RUSSIA’S PARLIAMENTARY ELECTION REACHES OCCUPIED UKRAINE The test will be whether the Student List can transition their popular mobilization in the streets into a viable political option that can win an election and govern a country that hasn’t undergone a political transition in over a decade. It’s also unclear, if the Student List were to win, how they might reorient Serbia’s foreign policy and its relations with the U.S. "So far, the students have been remarkably reluctant to define foreign policy goals that would depart from the current government’s course. For now, the most realistic expectation is continuity," Sinisa Vukovic, director of the Global Policy Program at the School of Advanced International Studies at Johns Hopkins University, told Fox News Digital. Vuković said that Serbia’s foreign policy has remained mostly consistent dating back to Slobodan Milosevic, the former leader of Yugoslavia, and the Vucic government has left hot-button issues including the crisis over Kosovo and EU membership mostly unresolved. While much might change in Serbia domestically, any resolution to the conflict with Kosovo or any substantial reorientation of foreign policy that shifts Serbia away from Russia and moves it much closer to the U.S. and EU remains unclear. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Another period of pseudo-hedging is likely, with Russia keeping a deep presence in the most vital sectors and dominating most of them," Vukovic added.

articles.title: Glasgow museums remove mummified remains from public view
articles.summary: Kelvingrove Museum and The Hunterian say they have removed human remains from display because of ethical concerns.
articles.body:
Two museums in Glasgow have removed the remains of Egyptian mummies from display over ethical concerns.

The mummified corpse of the priest Nekht was taken out of public view at Kelvingrove Gallery, while The Hunterian Museum has covered Lady Shep-En-Hor's body in a specially designed textile to protect it from being seen by visitors.

The institutions said the decisions followed a reassessment of their duty of care towards the deceased.

It comes after the International Council of Museums (Icom) revised its code of ethics, recommending that the "inherent dignity" of human remains be upheld.

Both museums said they would consider repatriation of the remains should they receive an approach from a country or institution.

Despite the new code of ethics, there is no uniform approach across Scotland's museum sector with different institutions given leeway on how to implement it.

A spokesperson for National Museums Scotland (NMS) said it was not considering any changes to the display of human remains in its collection.

NMS has a large collection of Scottish archaeological remains as well as mummified people from Egypt and Peru.

Glasgow Life, which manages Kelvingrove, said it had taken the decision to remove the painted coffin containing the remains of Nekht in the "absence of consent from the deceased individual or their ancestors".

Nekht is thought to have lived at some point between 1985 and 1797 BC and was excavated at Beni Hasan in Middle Egypt during digs carried out in the early 20th century.

The remains were donated to the city of Glasgow in 1923.

A spokesperson for Glasgow Life said the withdrawal of the remains "reflected contemporary museum practice".

They added a new draft human remains policy proposed that they were only displayed "where there is documented and informed consent from the deceased individual or, in appropriate circumstances, their descendants".

They said a parliamentary group on African repatriation had highlighted "ethical concerns" over the display of such remains due to the "constant disregard" of potential wishes and intentions of ancestors who buried them.

A mummified male head, right foot and a right hand recovered from the Valley of the Kings in Luxor were also taken out of public view.

The spokesperson added: "We believe removing ancient Egyptian human remains from display is more respectful to the deceased individuals."

Meanwhile, The Hunterian said it had sought advice from Egyptologists before protecting Lady Shep-En-Hor's remains as part of a "commitment to becoming a more ethical institution".

A spokesperson for the museum, managed by the University of Glasgow, said the conclusion of that consultation led to the view Lady Shep-En-Hor "deserved privacy in death".

Her ornate sarcophagus, which has been on display almost continuously since 1820, will remain on public view as a "fine work of late period ancient Egyptian funerary art".

Lady Shep-En-Hor has never been removed from the coffin, but has been X-rayed and CT scanned in the last 50 years.

In the 1970s, several theories were put forward questioning whether the remains in the coffin were actually those of Lady Shep-En-Hor.

The Hunterian said excavators in the 19th century occasionally swapped over remains from different coffins, with better preserved specimens placed in the most intact or ornate sarcophagi.

The Icom code, which was revised in June, states museums should "uphold the inherent dignity of human remains and promote respect for their significance".

It adds: "Decisions about these items and collections should be made in collaboration with descendants or communities from which they originate, if known."

Prof Steph Scholten, who sits on the Icom ethics committee, said the code was intended as guidance and the final decision ultimately rested with each individual institution.

He added: "What the code of ethics puts forward is that these topics need careful consideration and decision making, they do not suggest one fixed outcome.

"Kelvingrove and The Hunterian have come to slightly different outcomes about our displays.

"The code of ethics does not prescribe that all human remains should be taken of display."

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire for one city brokered by Melania Trump, White House says
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — U.S. first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said on Friday.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — U.S. first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said on Friday. Residents of the southern Ukrainian ⁠town, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis. “Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway,” a White House statement ⁠said. The development comes as Melania Trump’s husband, ​President Donald ⁠Trump, pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war, which began when Russia ⁠invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Melania Trump has been active in trying to get ​Ukrainian children ⁠seized by Russia during the ‌war returned to their families. “The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of ‌elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, ‌food, and clean water,” Melania Trump said in the statement. The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either ⁠Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed American media organization accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said. Ukraine’s top ⁠negotiator, David Arakhamia, said on Telegram that the humanitarian operation would ​start ⁠once a ceasefire was in place. He said the accord, the result of a long process involving Melania Trump and Pope Leo, would set up a humanitarian corridor for residents to leave and allow assistance into ⁠the town. The Kremlin on Friday confirmed the agreement and said that the Russian and Ukrainian militaries were working to determine the dates ⁠for implementing it. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Friday that all civilians ‌wishing to leave Oleshky ‌would be allowed to do so and that the evacuation operation itself was ⁠expected to take at least several days. Peskov praised Melania Trump’s role in securing the agreement, something he said had been discussed in a recent phone call between Russian President Vladimir ‌Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump. “We ​welcome the efforts of ‌the First Lady ⁠of the United States, Mrs Melania ⁠Trump, who has made a significant contribution to ‌the coordination ​of the humanitarian ‌operation,” Peskov said. Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to 2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before the war, ‌the White House said. About 90% of the city was flooded ​following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House. The ‌statement said Melania Trump and ⁠her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms ⁠of the localized ceasefire. “Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred ‌destination. I anticipate some ​will want to go to Russia, and ‌some to Ukraine,” Melania Trump said. Newsmax, a right-leaning news outlet, said in a report that its cameras would be granted “exclusive access to document the effort.”

articles.body: The Chinese woman who had five ribs broken by her husband's hug has reportedly been diagnosed with osteoporosis, reports claimed after the video went viral. But during the hug, the husband could hear a cracking sound and the video captured the wife immediately sitting down in pain. The man, surnamed Wang, said he did not even give a tight hug. Doctors did not recommend surgery as they believed medication, patches and rest would heal her.Wang said doctors diagnosed osteoporosis that explained his wife's fragile bones. Wang told local media that his wife weighed between 45 and 50 kg and did extreme dieting, mostly skipping dinner. She also had no exposure to sunlight, the husband said. The woman worked at the family's shop which was just two or three-minute drive from their home, he said.Yan Yanxiang, an associate chief orthopaedic physician at Wuhan Asia Heart General Hospital, told Jingshi Live that it was uncommon for younger people to suffer rib fractures from the force of a hug. articles.title: Climate lawfare's back-channel campaign, and how you'll pay the bill
articles.summary: The Federalist No. 78 promised judicial restraint, but documents reveal climate activists targeted federal judges to influence energy company lawsuits.
articles.body: In The Federalist No. 78, Alexander Hamilton famously promised that the federal judiciary would have "neither FORCE nor WILL, but merely judgment." The climate lawfare movement has spent the better part of a decade trying to prove Hamilton wrong. Earlier this month, the Supreme Court heard oral argument in Suncor Energy v. County Commissioners of Boulder County, in which Boulder seeks to use Colorado public nuisance law to make two energy companies pay for the effects of global climate change. The case is the culmination of a long campaign. SUPREME COURT BEGINS NEW TERM WITH HIGH-PROFILE LOOK AT CLEAN AIR AND FEDERAL AUTHORITY A small, well-funded network of climate activists, convinced that drastic action is needed to save the planet and frustrated that their fellow citizens have not voted to dismantle the fossil-fuel industry, have turned to state and local courts after the Supreme Court unanimously shut down federal climate-nuisance suits in 2011’s American Electric Power v. Connecticut. Their strategy rests on a single premise: When the front door of democracy is closed, try the courthouse back door. But thanks to documents released September 30 by the House Judiciary Committee, we no longer have to guess. One of the movement’s architects put the strategy in writing. CLIMATE SEMINARS FOR JUDGES FACE FUNDING TRAIL PROBE AMID FEARS OF OUTSIDE INFLUENCE ON COURTS "It seemed to me that without legislative or executive action to address the climate problem, real government action might still be derived from court decisions," Paul Hanle wrote in a May 2022 email. Hanle founded the Environmental Law Institute’s Climate Judiciary Project, which has put at least 140 federal judges through its climate "education" seminars. In the same email, he laid out CJP’s strategy to target "key judges" with seminars, hoping to "make a great difference in the final outcome of cases." The crown jewel was the judges’ own science manual. In December 2022, the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine invited Michael Burger to write the climate chapter of the Reference Manual on Scientific Evidence, the federal judiciary’s go-to science guide. Burger runs Columbia’s Sabin Center for Climate Change Law and is of counsel at Sher Edling, a firm representing many of the cities and counties suing oil companies. The Federal Judicial Center balked, citing his litigation work. CHINA-LINKED GREEN GROUP TRAINING US JUDGES DRAWS FRESH HEAT AS FOREIGN TIES FUEL PRESSURE AT HOME The next day, Burger told his Sabin Center colleagues, the chapter’s eventual named authors, that he’d "be happy to contribute behind the scenes." Within weeks, one of them was circulating a draft with "Mike’s edits" and revising the legal section in response to his comments. Soon after the manual was published, the FJC withdrew the climate chapter. The National Academies finally followed suit in August. Why all the stealth? Because climate plaintiffs have a causation problem they cannot solve in the open. SUPREME COURT CAN RESTORE SANITY AND STOP THE LEFT’S RADICAL CLIMATE AGENDA At the Suncor Energy oral argument, Justice Elena Kagan told the oil companies’ lawyer, "Well, you sound like you have a very good causation argument." She meant it as a brush-off; she immediately questioned why causation should matter for preemption. But Kagan is right: No climate plaintiff has a good causation argument. Greenhouse gases mix globally, and about 90 percent of emissions occur outside the United States. Tying a drought in Boulder to any particular company’s barrels of oil is simply not possible. ECO-WARRIORS WANT TO TURN UP THE HEAT ON YOUR WALLET TO FUND THEIR CLIMATE AGENDA That is why the climate lawfare movement needs judges to swallow "extreme event attribution." Boulder’s trial court has already shown what the endgame looks like, declaring, "in a multiple contributor tort case, there is no need to tie specific injuries to the actions of defendants." If you can’t meet the standard, lower it. This is precisely what the Constitution’s structure exists to prevent: a small minority weaponizing federalism to impose its policy preferences on the entire nation. One county cannot regulate the world. If Boulder prevails, the companies’ lawyer warned, some 90,000 municipalities could make national energy policy through jury awards. Pressed by Justice Clarence Thomas at oral argument, Boulder’s lawyer conceded that "nothing in our theory" prevents suing retailers too. WAVE OF OVERLOOKED 'LEFT-WING' LAWSUITS COULD COME WITH AN UNEXPECTED PRICE TAG FOR AMERICANS And it won’t stop with oil companies. The Climate Judiciary Project’s own curriculum for judges shows where this is headed. One module touts "source attribution" studies tracing nearly two-thirds of all carbon dioxide emitted since the 1750s to 90 fossil-fuel and cement producers. Then it turns to the dinner table: "Though its members have not yet been named as defendants in climate change lawsuits, the heavily concentrated industrial animal agriculture industry also has been subjected to source attribution analysis." Note the word "yet." The module is candid about the point of the exercise. These studies take an alleged problem that could be attributed to "several billion past and present human individuals" and reduce it "to one driven by a few dozen companies," which makes climate change "appear to be more amenable to traditional tort law adjudication." This is regulation by litigation, pure and simple. Punish the companies that supply Americans’ fuel, food and building materials, and every family pays the bill at the pump and the grocery store. Chief Justice John Roberts cut to the heart of the matter: "Isn’t your suit an attempt to evade those decisions?" He meant the Court’s long line of cases treating interstate air pollution as a matter of federal law, which Justice Brett Kavanaugh had called "a wall of precedent." Kavanaugh then read aloud from Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg’s opinion in AEP: Federal judges "lack the scientific, economic, and technological resources" to set emissions policy. If that is true of federal judges, Kavanaugh asked, doesn’t it apply to "a six-person state jury in Boulder?" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Take it from Ginsburg herself. The climate lawfare complex lost at the ballot box. It lost in AEP. So its backers went behind the scenes—into judicial seminars and judges’ own science manual. Enough already. articles.title: Trial set for men accused of Manchester synagogue bomb plot
articles.summary: The Iranian men are alleged to have identified Heaton Park Synagogue and the Jewish Museum as targets.
articles.body:
Two Iranian men have appeared in court over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb.

Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, are accused of conducting hostile reconnaissance at Heaton Park Synagogue, which was subject to a fatal attack last year, along with the Jewish Museum in Cheetham Hill.

The pair, who arrived illegally into the UK on boats, are charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts on or before 20 September. They deny the charges.

They appeared via videolink at the Old Bailey and a trial date was set at Manchester Crown Court for 15 June 2027.

It is alleged Ahmadyan and Salehi were in contact with an Iranian national who directed and co-ordinated the planned attack, with the third party most likely operating within Iran.

The men are accused of getting instructions to make a chlorine bomb and acquiring liquids, components and equipment required in order to manufacture or assemble an improvised explosive device.

They are also accused of using the internet to identify and research potential targets, acquiring images, plans and maps of potential targets and conducting reconnaissance of potential locations for attack.

The trial is estimated to last five weeks. The next court hearing is due to take place on 16 April next year.

Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue on 2 October last year, and began a knife attack while wearing a fake suicide belt.
