articles.title: Plans for AI data centre in Canterbury approved by council
articles.summary: There are concerns about water usage, but the company said it would be within suggested limits.
articles.body:
Plans for an AI data centre in Kent have been approved by Canterbury City Council.

Era4, a British technology infrastructure company, sought planning permission for the site near the Shelford Landfill in Broad Oak, Canterbury.

The company said the brownfield site, previously used as a composting facility and now for general storage, provided an "opportunity to make efficient use of land and to connect to an on-site source of renewable energy".

Despite concerns around the plans' water cooling system and water usage, the council's planning committee approved it with four votes in favour, three abstentions and one against, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS).

During a council meeting on 21 July, councillor Ian Stockley said the plans seemed "incredibly wasteful of our natural resources".

Era4, who rebranded from Carbon3.AI in March, said its closed-loop cooling system would only be used in "periods when the outside temperature was above 25 degrees".

Its water usage statement said the proposed facility is expected to use up to 1804 gallons (8.2m³ ) a day, which it said remained below South East Water's suggested 4399 gallons (20m³) .

Councillor Michael Dixey said that "water usage is obviously a massive concern" and asked if a lower usage limit could be imposed.

Simon Thomas, head of planning at Canterbury City Council, said the proposed usage was "equivalent to about 60 households, so it's not a significant use of water comparatively".

Residents near Shelford Landfill previously said it had become a "mountain" of rubbish and caused a "sickening" smell .

articles.body: Former NFL star J.J. Watt turned a $100,000 donation into a massive relief effort after Hurricane Harvey devastated Texas in 2017. The Houston Texans defensive end launched an online fundraiser with an initial target of $200,000, but the campaign eventually raised $41.6 million, helping thousands of families recover from the disaster.Nearly a year after the hurricane struck, Watt’s foundation announced in August 2018 that the money had been distributed to organisations working to rebuild affected communities. The campaign remains one of the most notable examples of an athlete mobilising public support for disaster relief.According to the Houston Texans’ official website, Watt launched the fundraiser on August 27, 2017, while he was away from Houston during the storm. What began as a personal effort quickly attracted donations from more than 200,000 people across the United States and around the world.How J.J. Watt launched the Hurricane Harvey fundraiserHurricane Harvey made landfall in Texas in August 2017, bringing torrential rainfall and devastating floods to Houston and surrounding areas. The disaster damaged homes, disrupted essential services and left thousands of residents in need of emergency assistance.Watching the destruction unfold, Watt decided to use his public platform to raise money for the affected communities. He contributed the first $100,000 and set an initial fundraising target of $200,000.The response far exceeded expectations. Within weeks, the campaign had raised more than $37 million. By August 2018, after additional donations and checks were accounted for, the total had reached $41.6 million.In a statement explaining his approach, Watt said his priority was to ensure the money reached the communities most affected by the hurricane.“Throughout this decision-making process, what mattered to me most was ensuring that the entirety of the funds would be utilized here in Houston and the surrounding areas for those who were affected most by Hurricane Harvey,” he said, according to the Houston Texans’ report.Where the $41.6 million in donations wentWatt’s foundation worked with eight nonprofit organisations to distribute the funds and support recovery efforts. These included Americares, Feeding America, SBP, Save the Children, Habitat for Humanity, All Hands and Hearts, Boys & Girls Clubs and BakerRipley.The organisations focused on several urgent needs, including repairing damaged homes, restoring childcare centres, providing food and delivering medical and mental health services.The aim was not only to provide immediate assistance but also to help families and communities rebuild their lives in the months following the disaster.How the fundraiser helped Hurricane Harvey victimsAn update released by the Houston Texans in August 2018 detailed the impact of the donations. The funds had helped clean up, repair and rebuild more than 600 homes, while more than 420 childcare centres and after-school programmes were restored or rebuilt. These facilities served more than 16,000 children.The campaign also helped distribute more than 26 million meals to people affected by the hurricane. More than 10,000 patients received medicine, while over 6,500 people benefited from physical and mental health services.The results showed how the donations extended beyond emergency relief, supporting housing recovery, healthcare and essential services for families across the affected region.J.J. articles.title: One person killed in suspected ‘Islamophobic’ shooting near Paris
articles.summary: Antiterrorism prosecutors investigating motive of attack that seriously wounded five, including a 12-year-old girl.
articles.body:
A gunman has killed one person ⁠⁠and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in a possible Islamophobic “terrorist crime” in the Paris suburbs, authorities said.

An unidentified 39-year-old male suspect was taken into custody shortly after the attacks in the towns of Trappes and nearby La Verriere outside the capital on Friday.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the suspect fired at a children’s playground, a fuel station and a medical centre, the Reuters news agency reported. Three of the victims, including the 12-year-old girl, suffered life-threatening injuries, he said.

Nunez said the attack lasted less than 15 minutes and that the gunman appeared to have used “a military-grade weapon, or at least an automatic weapon”. Prosecutors were treating it as a “terrorist crime” and investigating whether it was racially or religiously motivated, he said.

Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh said the gunman “appeared to be firing at random and seemed intent on carrying out a massacre”.

“This was a terrorist attack with racist, likely Islamophobic, overtones,” he said.

Rabeh earlier said two of the victims were of African and North African origins.

French President Emmanuel Macron said national antiterrorism prosecutors had taken over the case.

“Our thoughts go out to the victims, their families, and all the residents of Yvelines. In this terrible ordeal, the Nation stands by their side,” Macron posted on X.

Separately, security was tightened ahead of protests that are expected across the country this weekend. Many of the demonstrations have been banned following burning and looting at protests last weekend.

Nunez said France would deploy 70,000 officers nationwide on Saturday, along with helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannon. In addition, elite police units will help secure public buildings, such as city halls, in a “highly mobile” security operation, he said.

Protests last week caused chaos, with people setting fires, storming public buildings, smashing shop windows, looting and clashing with police, in France’s most violent unrest in years.

Far-right politicians say the government has not cracked down hard enough on protesters, while left-wing groups say the security around demonstrations violates rights.

Demonstrators plan to take to the streets again on Saturday to denounce the high cost of living. Students, members of the Confederation of Labour, a national trade union and activists from the “yellow vest” movement, whose demonstrations against social injustice shook France in 2018 and 2019, are all set to join.

articles.title: Andrew can be called to give evidence in High Court fraud trial
articles.summary: The High Court trial involves allegations of fraud made by a wealthy Turkish woman against her former adviser.
articles.body:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor can be called to give evidence in a High Court trial involving allegations of fraud against a Turkish businessman, a judge has ruled.

Nebahat Isbilen, a Turkish national, alleges that Selman Turk, her former adviser, misled her over a £750,000 payment made to Mountbatten-Windsor in 2019.

The judge agreed to allow Turk, who denies dishonesty, to seek to call evidence from Mountbatten-Windsor in a trial in London expected to begin in November.

Mountbatten-Windsor repaid the money, and there was no suggestion of wrongdoing by the former Duke of York.

Ahead of the trial, Turk made a bid to be allowed to call Mountbatten-Windsor to give evidence.

In a judgment on Friday, Justice Adam Johnson agreed, allowing Turk to rely on a witness summary and seek to call evidence from the former duke.

Johnson said: "Given the seriousness of the allegations, both on their own terms and in light of their wider impact, fairness requires that Mr Turk should be afforded an opportunity of putting forward his own case, using the evidence he considers relevant and material."

The judge later said that his decision meant Turk could call evidence from the former duke, but that a witness summons "will likely" be needed to compel Mountbatten-Windsor to give evidence.

Johnson added: "It is highly unlikely that a person in the position of Mr Mountbatten-Windsor would wish voluntarily to provide a witness statement and give evidence at a trial in public proceedings involving payments made by the wife of a person said to be a political prisoner in Turkey, in connection with a dispute about the reason the payments were made."

Isbilen, who in 2022 was 77 years old, is from a wealthy family, but when her politician husband was jailed she wanted help moving her assets out of Turkey.

Lawyers for Isbilen previously told the court that tens of millions of her funds had been misappropriated, with Turk failing to explain where the money had gone.

In Friday's ruling, Johnson said it "has long been Mr Turk's case" that the £750,000 payment was made on Isbilen's own accord as she believed Mountbatten-Windsor could help with her husband.

articles.title: Babydoll singer becomes first Welsh artist to top UK singles chart in 15 years
articles.summary: Jamie Miller is the first Welsh artist since 2011 to earn a UK Number 1 single - after Sian Evans' feature on DJ Fresh's Louder.
articles.body:
Jamie Miller has become the first Welsh artist to top the UK singles chart in 15 years with his viral TikTok hit, Babydoll.

Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, narrowly beat Tate McRae and her single Housewife to claim the top spot on the UK Number 1 on Friday, according to the Official Charts Company.

The achievement means Miller is the first Welsh artist since 2011 to earn a UK Number 1 single - after Sian Evans' feature on DJ Fresh's Louder.

Miller, 29, told Charts: "I don't even know what to say other than thank you so much for getting me Number 1, this is the biggest thing that's ever happened to me in my life, I love you guys."

He is also the first solo male Welsh artist in 41 years to top the singles chart, after Shakin' Stevens' 1985 timeless festive hit, Merry Christmas Everyone.

Babydoll was released on 7 August - months after Miller considered quitting music - and exploded after actress Jennifer Love Hewitt posted videos which featured the track.

It sparked a TikTok dance trend and hit number one on the US iTunes pop chart, and earned Miller his first appearance on the US Billboard Hot 100.

Babydoll narrowly missed out on the top spot last week.

Miller, who previously told BBC Wales his dad is an Uber driver in Cardiff, launched his career nearly a decade ago as a 19-year-old, after coming third on the sixth season of The Voice UK.

Miller has also recorded a separate version of Babydoll with Off Campus star Antonio Cipriano, after initially joking about the idea on social media.

Cipriano told BBC Wales last week that Miller was "one of the best vocalists I've ever heard", adding he had been a fan of Miller's voice "for years".

Miller previously said his love for music began accidentally, after becoming "hooked" on singing following an audition for a primary school show.

He said he was "proud" of his new music and was excited to share his latest album with the world and to tour it – in particular, he said, to bring it to Wales.

The singles chart top five was completed by Olivia Rodrigo's remixed version of Expectations with Chappell Roan and Ashe's Stop The Wedding at number four.

Meanwhile, the albums chart saw Irish band Fontaines DC score their second number one album with Dopamine Chamber.

The record marked the third biggest opening week for an album in 2026, and is also the fastest-selling Irish studio LP in 15 years since Snow Patrol's 2011 Fallen Empires.

articles.title: Trump says Burnham is 'getting it done' after Jackdaw decision
articles.summary: The US president has praised Burnham after the government allowed gas drilling in the North Sea's Jackdaw field.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has praised Prime Minister Andy Burnham for the UK government's decision to approve production from the North Sea's Jackdaw gas field.

He said he had spoken with Burnham, telling reporters on Friday that the decision would "make the UK a very rich country".

Trump said: "The other prime minister, the previous man, Starmer. He's a very nice man, but he never got it done, and this one is getting it."

The decision had been subject to intense debate around its environment and economic impact and came after years of legal challenges.

Burnham announced the decision to approve the drilling of the Jackdaw gas field earlier this week.

Jackdaw is situated 150 miles (241km) east of Aberdeen and is operated by Adura, a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state energy firm Equinor.

Ministers said the first gas could be produced by the end of this month, helping heat millions of homes, and also announced the creation of a new energy wealth fund.

Environmental campaigners say the decision would hamper efforts to tackle climate change and make "no meaningful difference" to UK energy security.

Based on official forecasts for the amount of gas the UK will need over the next decade, that suggests Jackdaw has the potential to meet around 1.6% of total projected national gas demand between 2026 and 2036.

Operators say it could be connected to the Great British gas network within weeks and could produce gas for the next 11 years.

Trump responded to the decision on Friday, but appeared to confuse oil and gas.

He said: "They're opening up the North Sea oil. I've been after them to do that for two years."

Trump added: "Andy is getting it done, and I guess it's against the liberal principle, but he knows what's right. It's going to make UK a very wealthy country."

Earlier this week, on Wednesday, Trump said the decision was "great news for the wealth and prosperity" of the UK.

Writing on his Truth Social platform, Trump urged the UK to go "full blast" and called the North Sea "one of the greatest and most prosperous areas of oil in the world".

A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, which is located off the coast of Shetland in the North Atlantic.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused the prime minister of "dithering" on Jackdaw and said a ban on new oil and gas licences should be repealed.

However, Burnham said her party had "messed up" the original decision by not giving any regard to climate obligations - things he said "have to be considered in the round".

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said gas from Jackdaw would be in homes and businesses this month, but that it would not lower energy bills this winter.

She said the decision was "compatible" with legally binding climate commitments, adding: "We remain resolute in ending new licences for oil and gas and achieving net zero by 2050."

Environmental groups have criticised the Jackdaw approval. Areeba Hamid, the co-executive director of Greenpeace, said it was "the wrong decision" in terms of lowering energy bills, providing energy security, and addressing climate change.

Meanwhile, Oxfam said the government had "drilled straight through the UK's climate commitments".

However, Ukrainian officials maintained a day later that speed curbs remained in place.Trump defends Musk amid Ukraine disputeTrump also defended Musk, saying he trusted the billionaire to act fairly despite concerns over the influence a private company has over communications systems vital to Ukraine’s military.“Elon will never do anything wrong. I know him very well. He's a fair person,” Trump said.The dispute centres on Starlink, SpaceX’s satellite internet service, and Starshield, its military-focused communications system. Ukrainian officials have said restrictions on the military-grade system have disrupted the use of some drones operating behind Russian front lines and affected air defence systems used to counter Russian attacks.The restrictions have also fuelled tensions between Washington, Kyiv and Musk over responsibility for controlling access to the technology.Trump and Musk have had a turbulent relationship, including a public falling-out after Musk led the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which sought to cut government spending last year.Relations between the two have appeared to improve in recent months, with Musk attending a White House state banquet in September.You use AI every day. articles.summary: AP Police booked 17 people in 14 election-related incidents across eight districts; DGP Harish Kumar Gupta orders strict action and enhanced poll security.
articles.body: Vijayawada: The AP police on Friday booked 17 persons in connection with 14 election-related incidents reported across eight districts in the state. He stressed that the same standards would be applied to offenders belonging to all political parties.Issuing a stern warning to those planning, committing or instigating disturbances, the DGP said they were examining CCTV recordings, drone footage, body-worn camera recordings and videography at nomination centres, wherever available. articles.title: YSRCP seeks transfer of senior IPS officers over poll violence
articles.summary: YSRCP asks Andhra Pradesh SEC to transfer senior IPS officers and probe alleged police bias and poll violence during local body nominations in Kadapa, Annamayya.
articles.body: Tirupati: YSRCP has urged State Election Commission (SEC) to initiate transfers and appropriate disciplinary proceedings against senior IPS officers in Andhra Pradesh over alleged electoral violence and police bias during the local body elections.In a complaint addressed to the state election commissioner (SEC), Tirupati MP Dr M Gurumoorthy sought an independent inquiry into allegations of police bias and electoral violence, along with a thorough review of compliance with previous transfer directives.YSRCP has sent copies of the complaint to President of India, Chief Justice of India, the Union home secretary, Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) and Andhra Pradesh governor, seeking their intervention.The complaint details alleged incidents of violence, intimidation and obstruction of opposition candidates during the nomination period from Oct 16 to 18, particularly in Annamayya and Kadapa districts.Gurumoorthy alleged that on Oct 16, Rajampet MP and Lok Sabha panel speaker PV Midhun Reddy, along with YSRCP nominees, was waylaid and attacked by TDP activists, triggering chaos that prevented candidates from filing nominations at Punganur.He added that similar incidents of obstruction and attacks on YSRCP nominees were reported across Kadapa and Annamayya districts, including Pulivendula, Kamalapuram, Kadapa, Yerraguntla, Rajampet, Rayachoti, Badvel, Mydukur and Proddatur.Official nomination and withdrawal reports from these districts, the complaint said, reflected heavily skewed outcomes. In Kamalapuram and Badvel, valid nominations for chairperson and ward posts overwhelmingly favoured TDP candidates, while opposition representation was virtually absent.YSRCP representation specifically named deputy inspector general of police (DIG) Dr Koya Praveen, Annamayya district superintendent of police Dheeraj Kanubilli and Kadapa district superintendent of police Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath, seeking their immediate removal from election-related duties over the alleged concentration of violence in their jurisdictions.YSRCP also accused DIG Koya Praveen of allegedly making objectionable political remarks about MP PV Midhun Reddy’s character. The remarks reportedly circulated widely on social media, triggering criticism over the officer’s political neutrality.The complaint further called for a thorough administrative review of Dr Koya Praveen’s current deployment in light of a 2019 govt order (G.O.Rt.No.815) that had directed his removal from field duties to ensure electoral impartiality.The electoral process has also come under judicial scrutiny, with a writ petition (W.P. No. 30103 of 2026) filed before Andhra Pradesh High Court.In its Oct 15, 2026, order, the high court ruled that blanket directions to shift designated nomination venues could not be issued on the basis of mere apprehension. However, it allowed individual candidates facing credible threats to approach election officers seeking secure alternative locations to file their nominations.Invoking these legal avenues, opposition leaders are urging SEC to exercise its statutory powers, coordinate with Election Commission of India and state authorities, order a comprehensive independent inquiry, preserve CCTV footage and other electronic evidence, and enforce stringent security measures to restore public confidence and uphold the rule of law during the ongoing local body elections.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: Gunmen kill 7 at Christian church in Jordan in what king calls act of terrorism
articles.summary: King Abdullah II vowed the "harshest retaliation" after gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, killing at least seven.
articles.body: Multiple gunmen opened fire and killed at least seven people Friday at a church in Jordan in what the country's leader is calling a "terrorist attack." The shooting, which also left 34 injured, erupted during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 110 miles south of the capital, Amman. Karak is home to a minority Christian population. "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation. Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity," King Abdullah II wrote on X. "All Jordanians, from north to south, are partners in land and fate, and nothing stands between them. Our deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs and we wish a speedy recovery to those injured," he added. "Every Jordanian life is precious, and we will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation." TWO SUSPECTED GUNMEN DEAD, TWO IDF SOLDIERS KILLED IN WEST BANK SHOOTING Images broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots, according to The Associated Press. A third man who appeared to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then appeared and opened fire, and all three then ran toward the church. A government statement said that the attack was "carried out by unknown assailants" but didn't say whether any gunmen were captured or killed. It noted that "investigations are underway at full speed." 43 YEARS AFTER BEIRUT TERROR ATTACK KILLED 241 AMERICANS, RABBI RECALLS CHAPLAINS' EXTRAORDINARY RESPONSE In 2016, gunmen ambushed police in a series of attacks in Karak, including at a Crusader castle popular with tourists, killing 10 people, including seven officers, and wounding dozens. Jordanian security forces killed those gunmen after a long standoff. Jordan’s director of public security, Maj. Gen. Obeidallah Maaytah, said at a news conference that 27 of the wounded in Friday’s shooting were still being treated. articles.title: NDA unity faces grassroots test in GVMC polls as ticket discontent persists
articles.summary: NDA’s TDP-Jana Sena-BJP unity faces test in GVMC polls as seat-sharing disputes and rebel independents threaten to split votes in key wards.
articles.body: Visakhapatnam: The unity of the TDP–Jana Sena–BJP alliance is facing a crucial grassroots test in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections, with disgruntled aspirants and lingering seat-sharing differences threatening to complicate the contest in several wards.Nearly 260 Jana Sena aspirants filed nominations for the 120 wards, seeking tickets under the alliance banner. Although most aspirants who failed to secure official nominations later withdrew their papers, some are learnt to have remained in the fray as independents, potentially splitting the alliance votes in key wards.Effective coordination among the three partners will be crucial if NDA is to replicate its sweeping performance in the 2024 elections. The alliance won all assembly and Lok Sabha constituencies falling within GVMC limits, covering eight assembly segments and parts of two parliamentary constituencies. Visakhapatnam also recorded two of the highest victory margins among Andhra Pradesh’s 175 assembly constituencies, while TDP’s Visakhapatnam Lok Sabha candidate secured a majority of more than five lakh votes, the highest in the state.The three parties had largely worked as a cohesive unit during the 2024 elections, combining their organisational networks and grassroots influence. The civic polls, however, have exposed differences over ward-level representation and ticket distribution.Seat-sharing negotiations dragged on for several days, with an agreement emerging only on the final day of withdrawal of nominations. TDP initially proposed contesting 80 wards, allotting 30 to Jana Sena and 10 to BJP. Jana Sena and BJP leaders sought a larger share, citing their contribution to the alliance.Following negotiations, Jana Sena secured 32 wards and BJP 11, leaving TDP with 77. The allocation has reportedly left sections of both TDP and Jana Sena dissatisfied. Some TDP leaders feel Jana Sena has been allotted more seats than warranted, while some Jana Sena leaders believe the distribution is unfair in certain parts of the city. Visakhapatnam West, Visakhapatnam East and Pendurthi are among the areas where the differences are said to be particularly contentious.The final list of candidates in the fray is yet to be officially released in view of a court order. However, several TDP and Jana Sena aspirants who failed to secure official party nominations are learnt to have retained their candidature. Contesting as independents, they could dent the prospects of official alliance candidates in individual wards.One such candidate is Peethala Murthy Yadav, a Jana Sena corporator who was a vocal critic of the previous YSRCP govt and legally challenged the Rushikonda development project. Having failed to secure a party ticket this time, he is contesting as an independent from Ward 26, making it the ward to watch in the civic polls.Meanwhile, TDP and YSRCP have stepped up their campaigns for the mayoral post. Visakhapatnam MP M Sribharat, campaigning in the Neelamma Vepachettu area on Friday, appealed to voters to deliver a decisive mandate for alliance candidates, including mayoral nominee Mukka Sravani. He said a strong mandate would facilitate the implementation of development projects worth around ₹4,000 crore being taken up in the city.YSRCP mayoral candidate and MLC Varudu Kalyani campaigned in Madhavadhara on Friday, asserting that her party could steer the city’s development while ensuring that public welfare remained a priority.With seat-sharing discontent and rebel candidatures adding to the contest, the GVMC elections will test whether NDA’s success at the state and parliamentary levels can translate into a united electoral front at the ward level.NDA SEAT-SHARING IN GVMC80 wards | Initial TDP proposal30 wards | Initial allocation to Jana Sena10 wards | Initial allocation to BJP32 wards | Final Jana Sena allocation11 wards | Final BJP allocation77 wards | Final TDP allocationKey concern | Dissatisfaction over ticket distribution and independent candidates in some wardsYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: YSRCP moves HC, seeks extension of nomination deadline
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh HC adjourns YSRCP plea seeking 48-hour extension of MPTC/ZPTC nomination deadline amid alleged obstruction; next hearing Monday.
articles.body: Vijayawada: Andhra Pradesh high court on Friday adjourned to Monday a petition filed by YSRCP seeking directions to State Election Commission (SEC) to extend the deadline for filing nominations for MPTC and ZPTC elections by 48 hours in places where its candidates allegedly faced obstruction in submitting papers.YSRCP state general secretary Lella Appi Reddy moved the high court with a lunch motion petition for urgent hearing, seeking directions to SEC to extend the nomination deadline in affected constituencies and ensure protection to candidates in accordance with Supreme Court directions.Appearing for the petitioner, senior counsel S Sriram submitted that YSRCP candidates were being prevented from filing nominations in several places. He told the court that photographs and videos had been placed on record to substantiate the allegations and argued that candidates were being forced to approach courts merely to submit nomination papers.The counsel further alleged that false cases were being registered against YSRCP candidates and that efforts were being made to compel them to withdraw nominations. He contended that the situation would not have arisen had SEC taken timely action and sought a 48-hour extension of the nomination process wherever candidates were obstructed.Advocate general Dammalapati Srinivas, appearing for the state govt, opposed the plea, contending that the allegations were unfounded. He submitted that over 12,500 nominations had been filed by YSRCP candidates in the MPTC elections and argued that isolated incidents could not be used to portray a statewide problem. He also submitted that police protection was being provided to candidates facing difficulties in filing nominations in line with the directions of Supreme Court.The counsel appearing for SEC submitted that the commission had issued circulars directing authorities to personally escort candidates to nomination centres if they reported obstruction in filing papers. articles.title: Better civic planning tops Vijayawada’s municipal agenda
articles.summary: Vijayawada stakeholders urge long-term civic planning: improve drainage, water, traffic, parking and infrastructure in growing corridors; boost business consultation.
articles.body: Vijayawada: Vijayawada’s infrastructure challenge is no longer confined to its busy roads or waterlogged streets. As residential corridors expand and commercial activity grows, stakeholders say the city needs a more coordinated approach to civic development, one that plans for growth before infrastructure gaps become everyday problems.The concerns span three interconnected areas: the condition of basic civic services, the ease of doing business and the need to provide infrastructure in neighbourhoods where development is gathering pace. Stakeholders want the next municipal leadership to move beyond individual works and adopt a long-term plan for the city.C H Baburao, CPI(M) state secretariat member, flagged stormwater drainage, drinking water, public health and traffic congestion as key concerns. He also questioned the adequacy of funding for civic infrastructure and called for greater accountability and public participation in municipal decision-making.For businesses, congestion is not merely an inconvenience. Potluri Bhaskara Rao, president of AP Chambers of Commerce and Industry said inadequate parking near commercial establishments was affecting business activity. He called for better traffic management and a municipal administration that consults trade and industry representatives before introducing measures affecting them.Bhaskara Rao also sought scientific urban planning, improved connectivity, pollution control and investment in tourism and employment-generating activities, arguing that the city needs to strengthen its economic prospects alongside its physical infrastructure.The pressure is also visible in developing residential corridors. Dasari Rambabu, general secretary of CREDAI Andhra Pradesh and former president of CREDAI Vijayawada, identified Gunadala, Poranki, Kanuru, Tadigadapa, Penamaluru, Tadepalli and the Gannavaram side as areas requiring focused infrastructure upgrades.He said roads, stormwater drains, underground drainage, sewage networks and street lighting must keep pace with residential growth. articles.title: North or South Kolkata, Durga Puja revelry stays low in decibels
articles.summary: Kolkata’s Durga Puja 2024 saw lower noise levels across north and south areas, with sound limiters, fewer DJs at immersions, and tighter decibel rules.
articles.body: Kolkata: In a city where festivities have mostly witnessed blaring loudspeakers, booming music and sleepless nights, this year’s Durga Puja celebrations, including immersions, were largely quieter.Be it Behala, Dhakuria or Amherst Street, residents said there had been a decline in blaring loudspeakers and late-night music. The decibels remained low even at the immersion rallies as the DJ music systems weren’t played along.For 82-year-old Amiya Dasgupta, a Behala resident, the difference was particularly striking. In previous years, the elderly often found themselves helpless against the relentless amplification of music from neighbourhood pandals. This time, the celebrations were restrained.Young revellers like Radhika Sarkar of Dhakuria, too, did not necessarily miss the decibels.The subdued soundscape also followed the tragic stampede at Chorbagan on Oct 17 and prompted several puja committees to temporarily suspend public entry and review crowd-management measures.Partha Ghosh, a key organiser of Shiv Mandir Puja and general secretary of the Forum for Durgotsav, said, “The experience raised a larger question about the character of community celebrations: whether festivals could retain their grandeur without excessive amplification.”Many puja organisers, he claimed, this time effectively used sound-limiters.In north Kolkata, where neighbourhood pujas traditionally spill onto narrow residential streets, the relatively lesser-noisy puja was equally noticeable.Amherst Street resident, Mrityunjoy Sen, felt that reducing unnecessary amplification could make festivities more inclusive.Environmental crusader Naba Dutta, general secretary, Sabuj Mancha, stressed the need to distinguish between a genuine change in public behaviour and temporary restraint.The apparent reduction also comes against the backdrop of tighter restrictions in certain areas.In Bidhannagar, puja organisers had been instructed to observe a 70-decibel ceiling and stop using public-address systems after 10pm.For Kolkata, the bigger question is whether this quieter celebration marks a lasting cultural shift or merely an exceptional year. “Durga Puja can be a riot of colours, creativity and collective joy without becoming a riot of noise,” said Subhas Datta, another green crusader.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news.
